prompt:
Reddit post, r/houseplants.
Title: Can this peace lily be saved? I was gone for three weeks. I cut out dead parts and gave it a good soak.

Maybe about six hours ago? Last time I watered it was before I left, about 3ish weeks ago. My place is also dry with the winter settling in.

What is wrong with my plant?
answer:
**Underwatering. Three weeks without water in dry winter air left it bone dry and collapsed.** It can be saved: the crown and most stems are still green, and peace lilies bounce back from wilting well.

1. **Drain it today.** Leave it in the sink 30 minutes so excess water runs out the drainage hole. Then put it back on its saucer and empty any water that collects after 15 minutes. If the pot has no drainage hole, tip the extra water out.
2. **Give it 2–3 days** in bright, indirect light, away from heaters. Stems usually firm up within a day or two. Any stem still folded at a kink, or any leaf turning yellow or brown after that, won't recover. Cut those at the soil line with clean scissors (10 minutes).
3. **Check the soil weekly** with a finger. Water thoroughly until it drains when the top inch is dry. With dry winter air that will probably be every 5–7 days.
4. **Before your next trip,** water thoroughly, then loosely cover the whole plant with a clear plastic bag (a dry-cleaning bag works). Set it in bright light but out of direct sun. This slows drying a lot over 2–3 weeks.

Expect it to look sparse for a while. New leaves will come from the centre.
